ch13.headline: For the same “il”, four heads, four readings: the heaviest weight of the row ranges from <n>{max}</n> on “{maxWord}” to <n>{min}</n> on “{minWord}”.
ch13.intro: An attention grid captures only one kind of relation: here, the one that links “il” to its noun. A sentence holds many others. So a transformer computes several grids in parallel, each called a head, and every head reads the same sentence in its own way.
ch13.combine: The results of all the heads are then combined into one. Nobody assigns them a role: each head discovers its own during training. The plate below shows four of them, on the sentence we have followed from the start: the second is the grid of the previous chapters.
ch13.note: These four heads are illustrative: their rules are set by hand, whereas real heads learn their roles on their own and are rarely this clean.
